data.title: Truist Financial to sell $5.5 billion of auto loans amid overhaul
data.description:
Truist Financial said on Tuesday it has struck a deal to sell $5.5 billion of auto loans, as CEO Mike Lyons pushes to overhaul the U.S. bank and exit less profitable, non-core businesses.

Here are some key details:

  • The sale is expected to generate $5.2 billion in net proceeds for Truist and mark its exit from near-prime auto lending.

  • The Charlotte, North Carolina-based bank also said a broad strategic review was ongoing.

  • "There's a lot of urgency and intensity that's been added to this evaluation that really started earlier this year," Truist finance chief Mike Maguire said at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference on Tuesday.

  • During the second quarter, Truist discontinued marine and recreational vehicle loans and reduced originations in several other less profitable consumer lending units, such as prime and non-prime auto.

  • "In addition to implementing a more robust deposit gathering strategy, we also believe further divestitures are likely as Lyons repositions TFC for stronger growth and profitability over the next three years," RBC analyst Gerard Cassidy said.

  • Truist said it is pairing the transaction, which is expected to close this year, with a repositioning of its securities portfolio to offset the capital created from the loan sale.

data.title: Canada Looks to Lure New Investment With Aggressive, Broad Tax Writeoff Terms — Update
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart and Paul Vieira

Canada is implementing a tax change tied to the accelerated write off of capital equipment that attempts to move the country toward Prime Minister Mark Carney's goal of attracting nearly $1 trillion of new investment.

Lobbying groups for Canadian companies applauded the decision and said it could set the stage for an investment renaissance. Economists and public-policy analysts dubbed this the most substantial change to Canada's tax code in decades, and helps Canada compete following President Trump's tax revamp introduced last year.

Carney's announcement on Tuesday is aimed at strengthening Canada's tax competitiveness and encouraging investment at a time when Canada is confronted with a toughened trade environment and hefty tariffs on key exports to the U.S. Officials said the proposed change will improve productivity and strengthen the economy.

Dubbed the productivity-mega deduction, the government said it will allow for the immediate expensing of a broad-based range of depreciable property on a permanent basis. This would allow businesses to fully write off the cost of an investment in the year that it becomes available for use.

"Simply, your investment dollars will go a lot further in Canada than anywhere else in the advanced world," Carney told an audience at an investment summit in Toronto, where he hopes to match some of the world's biggest investors with Canadian companies pitching shovel-ready projects.

The big change, analysts said, is that officials are expanding the types of assets eligible for the accelerated writeoff. The writeoff was previously limited to assets in the manufacturing sector. That deduction can now be applied more broadly, to the energy and mining sectors and broadband for instance, thereby covering about two-thirds of all capital investment, officials said.

"This is a measure that helps address the single largest economic challenge Canada faces currently--productivity," said Trevor Tombe, an economics professor at the University of Calgary, adding business investment is the most important driver of productivity. Levels of productivity and business investment have been so lackluster that it prompted a senior Bank of Canada official in 2024 to declare the economic challenges a national emergency.

Carney said the expensing changes will position Canada as a tax-competitive leader for new investment, by offering the lowest marginal effective tax rate among Group of Seven nations. In charts accompanying his announcement, Carney said Canada's marginal effective tax rate--or the level of taxation from all levels of government on every additional dollar of capital spending--will now be less than half the U.S. rate, and roughly one-third of the average for Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development countries.

"We are making it cheaper to invest," the prime minister said. At a press conference, he said the government needed to offer immediate incentives to investors to accomplish its goal of building new trade corridors and resource projects that are necessary to restore economic resiliency.

"We need a clear advantage. We have a clear advantage now," Carney said.

Business Council of Canada chief executive Goldy Hyder said his group was pushing for such a move to be included in the government's upcoming 2026 budget plan. The measure "will help catalyze investment in Canada's capital infrastructure," said Hyder, who represents CEOs from the country's biggest corporations.

Candace Laing, head of Canadian Chamber of Commerce, said she expects the measure to "unlock investment and create jobs...The permanency of this deduction at these levels will draw the attention and interest of investors in Canada for longer than any investment summit could last."

The government estimates the incremental cost of the measure to be about C$36 billion, about $25.67 billion U.S., across five years from the 2026-27 fiscal year. Officials estimate the tax change could increase economic output by C$22 billion annually.

Write to Robb M. Stewart at robb.stewart@wsj.com and to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: Alex Saab, ally of Venezuela's Maduro, pleads guilty in US corruption case
data.description:
Key points:
  • Saab agrees to forfeit $195 million and cooperate with Justice Department
  • Prosecutors say Saab stole from Venezuelan welfare plan and moved proceeds to US accounts
  • Maduro is jailed without bail in Brooklyn ahead of June 2027 trial

By Luc Cohen and Jonathan Stempel

A Colombian-born businessman with close ties to ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro pleaded guilty on Tuesday in a U.S. corruption case, as federal prosecutors prepare separately to take Maduro to trial next year.

Alex Saab entered the plea to one count of money laundering conspiracy at a hearing before U.S. District Judge Kathleen Williams in Miami, court records show.

He also agreed to forfeit $195 million and cooperate with the U.S. Department of Justice. The court records did not reveal the nature of any investigations where Saab might offer help.

Saab's lawyers did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Prosecutors said Saab stole millions of dollars from a welfare plan intended to help feed needy Venezuelans, and transferred some proceeds to U.S. bank accounts.

He had pleaded not guilty in July, two months after being extradited as part of acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodriguez's attempt to shed parts of her predecessor's government.

Saab served under Maduro as Venezuela's minister of industry, before being removed by Rodriguez in January soon after Maduro's seizure by U.S. Special Forces in Caracas. Venezuela's new government detained Saab the following month.

The U.S. criminal case is the second against Saab.

In 2020, he was detained in Cape Verde and extradited the following year to face money laundering charges for allegedly siphoning $350 million out of Venezuela in connection with a bribery scheme.

Former U.S. President Joe Biden granted Saab clemency in December 2023, as part of a prisoner swap.

Maduro is being held without bail in a Brooklyn jail, after pleading not guilty to drug trafficking charges.

He has claimed immunity from U.S. prosecution because he once led a sovereign country. Legal experts have called this an uphill battle, in part because Washington had not recognized Maduro as Venezuela's president since 2019. Maduro's trial is scheduled for June 1, 2027.

data.title: Wells Fargo CFO Says the Bar for Bank Mergers Remains High — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Rebecca Ungarino

For months, investors and banking industry executives have privately speculated Wells Fargo could be poised to acquire a smaller lender.

The fourth-largest U.S. bank is no longer subject to the longstanding asset cap that limited its growth, and more broadly, regulators are signaling a willingness to push through bank mergers, the thinking goes.

Wells' finance chief threw cold water on the idea Tuesday while suggesting the firm could instead make a deal tied to payments or tech.

During Barclays' annual financial services conference, an analyst asked Wells CFO Mike Santomassimo if he is thinking about buying another bank, pointing to a recent article that suggested Wells had room to buy another lender.

Santomassimo downplayed that notion, and said the company is focused on organic growth with the ability to grow from within business lines.

"Could you see us do an acquisition that adds some kind of capability in the payments space, or tech? Maybe," said Santomassimo, who joined Wells six years ago from BNY Mellon, where he was CFO. "But I think, overall, there's a high bar for us to think about acquisitions."

Wells' rivals have recently acquired small companies in areas as varied as cybersecurity and perks for credit cardholders.

Last month, Citigroup bought Kard Financial, a start-up that works with financial firms to offer their customers rewards, in an effort to bolster its U.S. credit card business. In late July, Bank of America scooped up an England-based cybersecurity firm called MDSec Consulting Limited. Neither bank disclosed terms of their deals.

Shares of Wells were up 0.5% in volatile trading Tuesday as the S&P 500 fell 0.5%. Wells' stock is down 7% in 2026; the S&P 500 is up 11% this year.

Write to Rebecca Ungarino at rebecca.ungarino@barrons.com

data.title: Palantir Looks Cheap Among AI Software Stocks, UBS Says — Why PLTR Could Have More Room To Run
data.description:
Key points:
  • UBS raised its price target for Palantir, while maintaining a ‘Buy’ rating.
  • The brokerage believes Palantir deserves a premium for its exposure to AI, data, and modern defense technology.
  • 20 of 31 analysts tracked by Koyfin rate PLTR ‘Buy’ or ‘Strong Buy.’

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) looks relatively cheap compared with AI-linked software peers, according to UBS, which expects the stock to rebound as demand for its artificial intelligence-linked software services gains traction.

At the time of writing on Tuesday afternoon, PLTR stock was trading nearly 1.7% higher.

UBS Raises PLTR Price Target

UBS reiterated a ‘Buy’ rating on Palantir and raised its price target to $250 from $220, implying 44% upside from Monday’s close.

“Last week we attended Palantir’s AIPCon customer/leadership event … our view of Palantir as the best AI enabler in the market (making frontier models/AI useful in large enterprises) was if anything bolstered by these conversations [with Palantir executives and customers], and demand momentum seems robust,” the UBS analyst wrote in a report on Tuesday, according to a report in CNBC.

Palantir provides AI-integrated software platforms to clients including the Department of Defense, enabling users to analyze massive data sets.

Valuation Looks Attractive

PLTR stock now trades at 51 times expected free cash flow for 2027, despite Palantir having “the highest growth and margin profiles across software,” according to UBS.

At current prices, the stock is particularly attractive versus peers such as Snowflake and CrowdStrike, UBS wrote, as reported by CNBC.

The brokerage said the “valuation discount derives largely from investor concerns about a near-term growth rate peak and the potential that the model providers begin to target the data software layer.”

“Palantir deserves a material multiple premium given its leading position in three key growth areas – AI, data and modern defense tech, making it a relatively cheap stock,” the brokerage wrote.

PLTR Stock: Stocktwits Retail Sentiment

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for PLTR was ‘bearish,’ unchanged in the past 24 hours, while message volume remained ‘normal’ during the same period.

The UBS call matches the consensus on Wall Street. According to data from Koyfin, 20 of the 31 analysts covering PLTR rate it ‘Buy’ and ‘Strong Buy,’ while nine rate it ‘Hold’ and one each rate it ‘Sell’ and ‘Strong Sell.’

The 12-month average price target on the stock is $195.57, representing potential upside of nearly 13% from Monday’s close.

PLTR shares have declined nearly 7% year to date.

data.title: Soybeans, soymeal rise on US crush data; wheat turns higher
data.description:
By Julie Ingwersen

U.S. soybean futures rose on Tuesday as soymeal futures surged 2% after a monthly industry report showed a smaller-than-expected soybean crushing pace in August, analysts said.

A jump in crude oil prices lent additional support to soybeans and corn, both of which are used in the production of biofuels. Wheat futures also climbed.

As of 1:05 p.m. CDT (1805 GMT), Chicago Board of Trade November soybeans (SX26) were up 13 cents, or 1.0%, at $13.17-1/4 per bushel and most-active December soymeal (SMZ26) was up $8.50, or 2.4%, at $364.70 per ton.

CBOT December corn (CZ26) was up 2 cents at $5.35-1/4 a bushel and December wheat (WZ26) was up 6-1/2 cents at $7.28-1/2 a bushel.

Soybeans and soymeal futures hit session highs after the National Oilseed Processors Association said its membership crushed 205.456 million bushels of soybeans in August, an 11-month low, and soyoil stocks thinned to the lowest level since November 2024.

CBOT soyoil futures (BOZ26) pared losses and turned higher after the report's release.

"The broader edible oil complex continues to be supported by the increasing demand for biofuel globally amid the ongoing energy shock due to disruptions in both the Middle East and Black Sea," StoneX commodities economist Mike Castle said in a client note.

In South America, Brazil's 2026/27 soybean production is expected to reach 181.64 million metric tons, up 0.7% from the previous year, national crop agency Conab said, but the figure fell below the U.S. Department of Agriculture's current forecast for a 186 million-ton Brazilian crop.

Conab projected total 2026/27 Brazilian corn production at a record 148 million tons, above USDA's forecast of 139 million tons.

Wheat futures climbed as hopes of military de-escalation in the Black Sea faded amid further attacks on infrastructure. Prices had fallen a day earlier on an announcement by U.S. President Donald Trump that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt strikes.

"So far, this deal between Ukraine and Russia is just lip service," said Tom Fritz, a partner with EFG Group in Chicago.

Meanwhile, Algeria’s state grains agency OAIC bought about 500,000 metric tons of milling wheat in an international tender, European traders said.

Harvesting was underway in the U.S. Corn Belt. The USDA on Monday reported harvest progress at 8% for corn and 6% for soybeans, as of Sunday, ahead of their respective five-year averages of 6% and 3%.

data.title: Elastic Security Achieves the Only Perfect Score in the 2026 AV-Comparatives Endpoint Prevention and Response Test
data.description:
Elastic (NYSE: ESTC) today announced that Elastic Security achieved the only perfect protection score in AV-Comparatives' 2026 Endpoint Prevention and Response (EPR) Test, earning Certified Leader status, the highest distinction AV-Comparatives awards in the test. Elastic sits at the very top of this year’s Certified Leader group, with 100% Active and 100% Passive Response scores and the lowest modeled operational footprint of any product tested. This is the second consecutive year Elastic has earned Certified Leader status.

Elastic was the only vendor to block and report all 50 threats at the first phase of the test, before any progressed to Internal Propagation or Asset Breach. Elastic also had one of the lowest total costs of ownership (TCO) among the 14 vendors tested.

Prevention strength matters because AI-powered attacks no longer move at human speed. Adversaries now deploy automated toolchains that compress the time from initial access to lateral movement, data exfiltration, and persistence to minutes, not hours. At that velocity, detection and response alone cannot keep pace; the window to intervene after an intrusion begins is too narrow. Elastic stops more threats before they execute, matching machine-speed attacks with machine-speed prevention.

AV-Comparatives tested 14 vendors against 50 multi-phase attack scenarios built on techniques from the MITRE ATT&CK framework. Phase one covers the first three MITRE ATT&CK chain tactics: Initial Access, Execution, and Persistence. The scenarios included executables, scripts, Office add-ins, USB-propagated payloads, fileless execution techniques, AMSI bypasses, and EDR unhooking. This year’s test also incorporated AI-assisted development methods to build testing tools and scenario variations to better reflect how attacker tooling has evolved.

"Elastic Security achieved Certified Leader status in the AV-Comparatives EPR Test 2026,” said Andreas Clementi, Founder and CEO of AV-Comparatives. “The product prevented and detected every one of the tested attack scenarios already at the first stage of compromise with no operational accuracy costs and no workflow delays for the user. It is a clean, complete result that reflects real strength in enterprise threat prevention.”

“AI is compressing attack timelines, and security teams can’t afford more alerts to triage. They need to stop threats before they turn into investigations," said Mike Nichols, general manager, Security, Elastic. "Stopping every attack at the first phase of this test shows the strength of prevention in Elastic Security. A threat stopped at the endpoint is an alert that never opens, an investigation that never starts, and an incident that never escalates."

This result extends Elastic Security’s strong performance across recent AV-Comparatives testing. Across the last three Business Security Tests spanning 2025 and 2026, Elastic was the only vendor to achieve 100% malware protection in every cycle, including the most recent test covering March through June 2026, where Microsoft and CrowdStrike were among vendors tested.

Elastic Defend, Elastic’s native endpoint protection, is available for Windows, macOS, and Linux across cloud, on-premise, hybrid, and air-gapped environments.
